title: DeepMind's Gemini 4 Agents Make Quantum Algorithms 290x Faster
dek: Every gain was proven in the Lean theorem prover, not just trusted.

facts.label: Qubits needed for drug enzyme P450

caption:
AI agents just did real quantum research, and they had to prove every answer. 🧠

Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI set teams of Gemini 4 agents loose on known quantum circuits for fusion energy, drug design and core quantum math. Every four hours the teams met at a virtual conference to swap ideas. The results: an 11.8x cheaper fusion simulation, 8x for a light-sensitive molecule, 2.5x for the Cytochrome P450 enzyme, and a 290x speedup on an arcsin routine.

The twist: these circuits are too big to simulate or run today, so each improvement had to be formally verified in the Lean theorem prover before it counted. DeepMind is open-sourcing the Lean quantum library and verified solutions on GitHub.

The gains still exceed what early error-corrected quantum computers can handle, but at AI Parabellum we see a bigger story: a working recipe for trustworthy AI-driven science.

What if AI could do research you can't test, and you could still trust it? DeepMind's answer: make Gemini 4 agents prove every result in Lean.

The payoff was quantum algorithms for fusion and drug design that run 2.5x to 290x cheaper, with the code going open source.
